kids.text: War Room Intelligence
Era 2 Update: Events, Mercenaries, Alliances & More
NEW
NEWS
So it's been a pretty active few weeks for OpenThrone since the fresh Era 2 release and so I figured it's probably great to go ahead and follow up on some changes.

There are some new systems, expanded upon existing ones, reworked some mechanics, and fixed a number of issues along the way. Not all of the features may remain or they may get branched off to being upgrades to unlock later or funneled into other avenues. I'm hoping that they are well received and show that there's still quite a bit more we can do to bring back and improve upon the old DT nostalgia while still staying relatively faithful.
Rather than making everyone dig through individual updates, here's a breakdown of what's changed and what you can expect during Era 2.
TL;DR
Game Events: Active players who logged in within the past 24 hours get 100 bonus citizens per day. More event types are planned.
Attack Recommendations: An Era 2 experiment that uses recent battles and spy reports to help you decide whether an attack is worth it. It won't guarantee a win.
Mercenaries: Hire fully equipped troops for offense, defense, spying, or sentry duty on 1, 3, or 7-day contracts. They're available for testing now, with progression-based unlocks planned later.
Alliances: Shared treasuries, loans, taxes, dues, war levies, and troops you can donate or borrow. There are also new tools for sharing intelligence, managing members, and coordinating attacks.
Combat and protection: Attacking no longer removes new-player protection. There are also changes to spying, battle reports, loot calculations, and recruitment limits.
UI and bug fixes: Better mobile layouts, training controls, translations, and accessibility, plus fixes for banking, upgrades, alliances, logins, and era resets.
Table of Contents
Game Events Are Here
Attack Recommendations (Era 2 Experiment)
Mercenaries Are Now Available
Alliances Got a Pretty Significant Overhaul
Alliance Treasury, Loans & Gold Management
Alliance Taxes, Dues & War Levies
Alliance Troops: Shared Military Forces
Intelligence, Diplomacy & General Alliance Improvements
Combat, Spying & New-Player Protection
UI Improvements, Quality of Life & Bug Fixes
What's Next?
Game Events Are Here
I've finally introduced Game Events, which allow us to run temporary bonuses and modifiers throughout an era. Think of things like 2XP weekends, Firesale (reduced prices), and more.
Our first event is already active: players who have logged in within the past 24 hours receive an additional 100 citizens per day.
It's a fairly simple event to start with, but the underlying system opens up quite a few possibilities.
Future events could include increased XP, faster population growth, bonus recruitment, additional gold or turns, discounted armory equipment, reduced training costs, and more.

Events won't necessarily be limited to giving everyone free resources, either. We can use them to shake up the pace of an era, encourage certain activities, or give players a chance to catch up or prepare for larger conflicts. My hope is to use them around holidays, get more engagement in certain weeks, test new features, and when an Era comes around we can do things like DarkCurse or the like, really change things up.
You'll find currently active events in the game's sidebar. I haven't quite figured out a more polished location for this, so suggestions are welcomed.
Attack Recommendations (Era 2 Experiment)
Another fun experiment that I always wanted from DT was to have Attack Recommendations, which we're now testing as a limited-time feature during Era 2.

The idea is simple: rather than having to manually compare every recent battle and spy report, the game can look at the information you already have and give you a general recommendation about attacking a particular player.
You'll find it beneath the Attack button.
Depending on your available intelligence, it may suggest that conditions look favorable, recommend a more limited attack, or advise caution.

Recommendations use your recent battles against that player, along with any spy reports you have access to from the past 24 hours. You can also open the underlying reports to see what the recommendation was based on.
This isn't a guaranteed win predictor.
It doesn't calculate some magical win percentage, know exactly what your opponent has right now, or tell you how many turns to commit.
It's only as useful as the intelligence behind it. If your last spy report is several hours old and your opponent has been online since then, their military could look completely different.

For now, I'm keeping this experimental while we see whether it actually adds something useful to the game. The goal is to help players make more informed decisions, not replace the strategy involved in making them.
Mercenaries Are Now Available

Mercenaries have made their way into OpenThrone and are currently available for testing, including to lower-level players during Era 2. I couldn't find much information on how Mercenaries operated in DT so I've taken some liberties here.
This early access is temporary. In a future update, mercenaries will become something you unlock through normal game progression and will come with limits provided by your Mercenary camp.

Unlike regular troops, mercenaries come fully equipped and ready to fight. You can hire them to supplement your offensive army, bolster your defenses, or provide additional spies and sentries. However, they are also not equal to regular fully equipped troops. Level 1 Offense Mercs are a bit stronger melee power than a Level 1 Offense, however they are weaker at shielding, which will lead to them causing more kills but also dying more.
They're also not permanent troops.
Mercenaries operate on contracts, with options to hire them for 1, 3, or 7 days. You can view when their contracts expire and pay to extend them if you want to keep them around.
They're still subject to casualties and wounds, and once their contract expires, their service ends.

This adds another consideration when managing your army. You might hire additional offensive troops for a short campaign, reinforce your defenses while you're vulnerable, or bring in extra spies before making a move against another player.
Of course, that also means keeping an eye on the cost. Hiring a mercenary force is one thing; paying to keep it around is another.
We'll be watching how mercenaries affect combat, progression, and alliances throughout Era 2 before deciding on any further adjustments.
Alliances Got a Pretty Significant Overhaul
Alliances are likely my largest area of focus since the last release, and one that will continue my focus in future releases.

Alliances have historically had limited impact beyond the member list, so they never got a true release. I've been expanding what you can do in an alliance to where I feel being a part of an alliance can have a meaningful impact on gameplay.
This includes considerably more functionality towards managing members, sharing resources, coordinating attacks, gathering intelligence, and building a military force.
Alliance Treasury, Loans & Gold Management
Alliances have a new shared treasury that members can contribute their gold towards.
Depending on their permissions, members can manage treasury transfers, request funds, approve requests, and issue loans.
Loans have repayment terms, giving alliances a way to loan gold to members without just handing it over.

Say one of your members is just a few gold short of an important upgrade, instead of having to wait a few days to save up the required gold the alliance could provide funding right away, and the member could pay the alliance back later.
I've added permissions for managing, request approvals, and if certain ranks can approve their own requests.
Alliance Taxes, Dues & War Levies
In addition to the treasury, alliances have a few ways to organize contributions from members.
Pillage Taxes: Role based contributions from gold gained from attacks.
Recurring Dues: Recurring contributions from either gold or equipped troops.
War Levies: A one time request to selected members with a due date.
Members can view what they owe and make partial payments while leadership can set contribution policies and what to do with members that haven't paid their dues.
Now alliance doesn't mean every alliance needs to start taxing their members into oblivion.

An alliance might just be about voluntary contributions, or use a small percentage from pillage funding for loans or military upkeep. Another might just ask for extra contributions when they intend to call upon members for a war.
However alliance you use it is up to the alliance and leadership to decide how they want to handle it.
Alliance Troops: Shared Military Forces
Members can now contribute equipped troops to a shared alliance reserve, forming the alliances own military force.
These donated troops are the property of the alliance, not the member.

Once in the reserve, eligible members can borrow the troops for a certain amount of time. Depending on the alliances settings, this can require the approval of leadership or just have a rank based allowance to use the reserve troops.
Deployments can be renewed and leadership can recall deployed troops at anytime.
If the deployed troops suffered casualties, those losses will be accounted for and the remaining troops will return to the reserve upon deployment end, but the wounded will require to recover.
There are restrictions to prevent using borrowed alliance troops to attack or spy on members of the alliance that donated the troops.

I'm curious to see how alliances end up using this. Members could focus on building and donating troops and let other members take care of the fighting or keep a reserve of troops to bolster members that are being attacked.
An alliance could raise up a fairly decent military reserve and rotate deployments between members depending on who is preparing for attack.
Intelligence, Diplomacy & General Alliance Improvements
I've also made quite a few alliance changes.
Members can share battle and spy reports and calls for attacks, farming, and reconnaissance.
Alliances can maintain Farm, Hit, and Block lists with corresponding badges on the attack lists.
New diplomacy tools for managing allies.
Announcements and chat notices for important activity.
More options for controlling what individual members and ranks are allowed to do.
Improved invites, leadership transfers, and general membership management.
Infighting: A tab and an additional confirmation when trying to attack a member of your own alliance.
Players can now belong to up to three alliances at once, although you can only lead one alliance.
There is still quite a lot to do for alliances but they are finally at a point where members can contribute more than just their name to the alliance.
Combat, Spying & New-Player Protection
I've made a few changes to combat, as well as how new-player protection works.
Attacking another player no longer strips away your new-player protection.
Eligible players who previously lost out on new-player protection by attacking during Era 2 have had it restored.
The sidebar now has a protection meter to see how close you are to reaching the time, population, or level limits to end your protection.
Citizens earned from Game Events also contribute to the population allowance used for the protection system, so receiving bonus citizens won't immediately work against you.
Other combat and intelligence changes include:
Attack and Spy screens now support sliders and exact numbers with summary before commit.
Successful spy missions no longer lose spies.
A spy force larger than the defending sentry force will result in success.
Spy reports show defensive strength vs actual defensive troop strengths.
Equipment information is organized against the appropriate troop roles.
Battle reports show when a player levels up.
Protected-player loot calculations have been fixed and adjusted.
Recruitment from signed-in accounts and external recruitment links now have separate daily limits and more clear information about recruit opportunity.
A few of these were balance changes and other fixes for mechanics that didn't quite work as intended.
UI Improvements, Quality of Life & Bug Fixes
There's been quite a bit of work on the less exciting areas of the game, mostly clean up existing pages, fix inconsistencies, and reported issues.
You'll likely see more consistent styling throughout the game including race themed elements, dialogs, tables, and notifications.
Tables should be more mobile friendly, upgrade lists now tell you what is next, and I've fixed some loading issues where pages would momentarily show incorrect values or zeroed out.
Quantity controls are more consistent with additional Max buttons. Training has Clear and Clear All options, and Max considers gold already committed to training queues.
I've expanded German and Spanish translations, and improved things related to keyboard navigation, screen readers, and reduced-motion support.
As far as bug fixes go, I've fixed issues related to:
Proficiency-point crashes
Bank withdrawal displays and transaction history paging
Housing upgrades
War history
Assassination targeting
Player profile population values
Alliance requests and settings
Loan terms
Friends and Enemies not loading correctly
Duplicate training and upgrade submissions
One particularly annoying issue was with shared rate limiting, which could potentially block completely unrelated players from logging in or attacking at the same time, which has now been fixed.
Era transitions have gotten some reliability fixes, especially related to ensuring battles aren't carried over when an era is reset.
What's Next?
Era 2 is giving us an opportunity to put some of these larger systems into actual gameplay and see how they hold up.

Some features, like mercenaries and Attack Recommendations, are still being evaluated. Others, particularly the expanded alliance mechanics, introduce quite a few new ways to play that will probably need adjustments as people start using them.
I'm especially interested in seeing how alliances approach shared armies, taxes, loans, and coordinated attacks once players have had some time to work with them.
As always, if something feels unbalanced, confusing, broken, or just doesn't make sense, let us know.
There's plenty more to work on, but for now, enjoy Era 2 and good luck out there.
